Granblue Fantasy nPake NATIVE

A desktop wrapper for Granblue Fantasy. This build is an experiment: the sidebar, the wiki and this page live in their own webviews beside the game, not inside Granblue's document. The game itself runs exactly as Cygames served it — nothing here modifies it.

Two clients

Granblue serves two different clients, and Options chooses which one to ask for. Switching restarts the app.

  • Mobile (the default). A lighter client with no chat column, laid out at a fixed width. It never reloads when you resize the window, which is why it is the default. Game size in the sidebar picks Large or Small — that is this app zooming its own webview, not a Granblue setting.
  • Desktop. The PC client, with its own Window Size settings in Granblue. Layout / Lock and the sidebar's Back and Reload appear only here.

Things you may not have noticed

  • Drag to scroll. Click and drag anywhere that already scrolls — the game's own pages as well as this sidebar — and it scrolls with the drag, with momentum. A drag never activates the control underneath it.
  • Locked mode (desktop client). Opening a panel hides Granblue's chat column (Alt+L does the same by hand) so the panel uses that space instead of squeezing the game. The mobile client has no chat column, so there is nothing to hide.
  • The wiki keeps its place. Close and reopen it and you are on the same page, at the same scroll, because its webview is hidden rather than destroyed. Opening this page or Options cannot wipe it — the wiki has a webview to itself, and About and Options share a second one between them.
  • The sidebar follows the game. Shortcut rows light up to show where you are in Granblue. The sidebar reads the game's address; it never writes to it.
  • Back and Reload (desktop client) sit at the bottom of the sidebar and drive Granblue, not this page. Alt+Left and Alt+R still apply to whichever webview has focus, on either client.
  • Panels can sit on either side of the sidebar. Options has the choice: right of the sidebar (the default, so the rail stays against the game) or between the game and the sidebar.
  • Three themes. Midnight, Ember and Tide, in Options. They tint this app's own chrome only — the sidebar, Options and this page. Granblue is never themed.

Limitations, and why

  • On the desktop client with Automatic Resizing, the sidebar and panels are hidden so Granblue has the whole window, and nothing of this app runs in the page. That mode re-fits and reloads on every width change, so anything placed beside it would fight you. The mobile client never re-fits, which is why it is the default.
  • macOS and Linux are untested in this experiment. The shipping client is also unverified there.

Granblue is never modified

The game runs in the form Cygames served it. This app reads the game's layout where it must, and in locked mode hides the chat column with CSS display alone. It never changes Granblue's settings, its code, or what it sends and receives.

The one thing it does ask for is which client to be served: the mobile option sends a phone User-Agent with the page request, exactly as a phone browser would. That is a request for a version Cygames already publishes, made before the page exists. Once the page arrives it is left alone — no scripts rewritten, no traffic altered, nothing injected to "make it mobile."
